statement_record.book: For a preorder (P, <=): (1) the principal set up(p) := {p' in P | p <= p'} is an upper set for every p; (2) p |-> up(p) is a monotone map from P^op to U(P), the upper sets ordered by inclusion; (3) p <= p' iff up(p') is contained in up(p) -- the Yoneda lemma for preorders, saying an element is determined up to equivalence by its web of relationships to all others; (4) draw the map for b >= a <= c.
statement_record.intree: `Covariant_Yoneda_Embedding (C : Category) : forall A B : C, Copresheaves [Hom B,─] [Hom A,─] ≊ A ~> B` -- the morphisms A ~> B are in setoid bijection with the natural transformations Hom(B,-) ⟹ Hom(A,-); carried by `Curried_Hom C : C^op ⟶ [C, Sets]`, whose value at x is the functor y |-> hom C x y acting by post-composition, and which is asserted Full (Functor/Hom.v:96) and Faithful (:85).

verifier.notes: CONFIRMED PRESENT. Blind pass reached PRESENT with the same evidence. Instance/Discrete.v:52 `DiscreteCat_Functor {A : Type} {C : Category} (f : A -> C) : DiscreteCat A ⟶ C := {| fobj := f; fmap := fun x y (e : x = y) => match e with eq_refl => id end |}` and :37 `DiscreteCat (A : Type) : Category := {| obj := A; hom := fun x y => x = y; homset := Morphism_equality; id := eq_refl; compose := eq_trans |}` are both verbatim at the cited lines; the file is registered (_CoqProject:182). ONE REFINEMENT the classifier's presentation note stops short of, which sharpens rather than overturns: DiscreteCat's hom-setoid is `Morphism_equality` (strict equality OF equality proofs, per the header at :17-21), not the trivial thin setoid a Proset uses, so for a general Type A without UIP `DiscreteCat A` is the path category rather than a thin/discrete preorder. Conversely, `Proset` instantiated at `eq` (never done in-tree, as the record notes) carries the trivial hom-setoid `fun _ _ => True`, so its fmap_respects obligation would demand that ALL proofs of x = y be sent to ≈-equal morphisms -- i.e. it needs UIP on A. On sets, the book's setting, the two readings coincide and the book's hypothesis ('<= is =') and conclusion (monotonicity is vacuous, the only relation being reflexivity, which goes to id) are matched exactly, so PRESENT stands; the caveat is that the identification 'DiscreteCat A = the discrete preorder on A' holds only up to UIP on A and is nowhere stated in-tree.

Program Definition Proset {A : Type} {R : relation A} (P : PreOrder R) : Category := {| obj := A; hom := R; homset := fun A B => {| Setoid.equiv := fun _ _ => True |}; id := fun x => @reflexivity A R (@PreOrder_Reflexive A R P) x; compose := fun x y z f g => @transitivity A R (@PreOrder_Transitive A R P) x y z g f |}.  -- the preorder IS the full relation R (already transitive), not a diagram of generators: composition is transitivity, so any transitively implied arrow is present whether or not it is drawn

statement_record.book: Three five-element preorders P (a..e), Q and R (v..z) are drawn; all are isomorphic, and the explicit map f : P -> Q with f(a)=v,...,f(e)=z has an inverse, hence is an isomorphism in the sense of Definition 1.75. Q and R are in fact the SAME preorder: the extra drawn arrow x -> z in R is superfluous, transitivity already forcing x <= z from x <= y and y <= z (likewise v -> y could be drawn in either). Moral: a preorder is not its Hasse diagram.
statement_record.intree: `Proset ... := {| obj := A; hom := R; ... compose := ...transitivity... |}` -- the carrier of the construction is the relation itself, with composition given by transitivity -- and the concrete witness `poset_nat_comp_0_2 : 0 ~{Poset_nat}~> 2 := compose poset_nat_hom_1_2 poset_nat_hom_0_1`, the implied arrow obtained from the two adjacent ones.
